title: Changing Momentum: Force and Time Practice

questions.question: To change momentum, what must act on an object?
questions.explanation: Impulse is force acting over time.

questions.question: For the same momentum change, increasing stopping time usually makes force
questions.explanation: Spreading the change over more time lowers average force.

questions.question: Pulling your hands back while catching a ball reduces the force on your hands.
A change in momentum can happen without any force.
questions.explanation: A force is needed to change momentum.

questions.question: Force applied over time is called ________.
Why should a catcher move their hands backward when catching a fast ball?
questions.correctAnswer: A good answer mentions longer stopping time and lower force.
questions.explanation: Moving the hands backward increases stopping time, reducing the force felt.

questions.question: Which statement best matches this lesson?
questions.explanation: The first option states a central idea from the lesson.
options: Changing momentum requires force acting during a time interval.
